review_notes:
I read the whole file and checked it against the repeated-proof-machinery rubric.

Candidates I considered and rejected:
- `finite_addMonoidHom` and `natCard_addMonoidHom_zmultiples_le` both inject a hom set into an n-torsion subtype of Q. The shared step is only "n • a = 0 implies n • φ a = 0", which is `map_nsmul` plus `map_zero`. The two injectivity arguments differ: one is by `ext` on all of A, the other uses `zsmul` on the generator. A shared lemma would save little.
- `natCard_addMonoidHom_le` (the `h2` block) and `natCard_le_natCard_addMonoidHom_quotient_orthogonal` both build an injective map into a quotient hom set with `QuotientAddGroup.lift` and `DFunLike.congr_fun`. They use different domains and different injectivity reasons: the kernel of the restriction map versus the nondegeneracy of β. The common part is routine unfolding, so a helper is not justified.
- The `natCard_sq_le_of_isotropic_*` corollaries and `encard_torsion_*` lemmas are thin wrappers around existing API. They are not repeated proofs of nontrivial reasoning.

I did not look for existing Mathlib lemmas, since no duplicated block seemed worth extracting. I found no repeated nontrivial proof that satisfies the rubric.
